parole.testo: From Persian آبزن (âbzan), from Middle Persian.

In the long form from Persian بادرنگبویه (bâdrangbôya), بادرنگبویه (bâdrang-bôya, “melissa”, literally “citron-smelling”) from بادرنگ (bâdrang, “citron”) + بوییدن (bôyidan, “to smell”), thought together with بورنک (bôrank), بورنگ (bôrang, “basil-royal”) implying “citronated basil” or “citrus basil”.
Arabic sources claim it is Persian, and Persian ones that it is Arabic (which often means it is from Middle Persian or Early New Persian and reinvigorated in Persian from Arabic).
